description: RAG over a mixed-filetype corpus. SAMPLE set; the graded set is different and harder.
answer_rule: Answer with the value only — a number, a part number, a version or a quarter. Cite the corpus-relative path of every file the answer came from. If the corpus does not contain the answer, return an empty answer and no citations; do not guess.

queries.query: What is the maximum junction temperature of the TQ-40?
queries.note: The WITHDRAWN r1 datasheet says 105 C. Citing r1 is wrong even though it is a real file with a real number in it.

queries.query: In which quarter does the TQ-60 enter customer sampling?
queries.note: This was the memory-capacity question until 2026-09-16. It was swapped because NO query cited the .docx, so a submission that could not parse Word documents still scored 10/10 -- the corpus listed a required file type it never actually tested. The capacity question was the most redundant one to give up: query 1 already exercises the same file and the supersession trap.

queries.query: What is the part number of the field-replaceable fan assembly for the TQ-40?
queries.note: A legacy single-rotor fan for the TQ-20 is the near-miss row.

queries.query: Which firmware version fixed ticket ORR-1847?
queries.note: The release notes are the near-miss: topically the most release-ish file in the corpus, and they retrieve well for this question. They no longer contain the answer token itself — see _txt() for why that decoy was dropped.

queries.query: What error code is logged when the thermal throttle engages?
What is the default batch timeout, in seconds, in the ingest service?
queries.note: A comment names the old value of 60. The constant is the answer.

queries.query: Which backplane pin carries THERM_ALERT# on the TQ-40?
queries.note: This value appears nowhere in any text file.

queries.query: What board revision is printed on the asset label?
The production log shows a thermal throttle incident. Which firmware release fixed the underlying defect?
queries.note: The log names the ticket; only the bug database carries the fixed-in version. Neither file alone answers this, and the database row is deliberately worded so that the question's own terms do not retrieve it -- the ticket id in the log is the only route. Verified 2026-09-16: before that rewording the row matched directly and the question was single-hop wearing a multi-hop costume.

queries.query: What is the unit price of the TQ-40 at 10,000 unit volume?
queries.category: refusal — the answer exists only in the ENCRYPTED file
queries.note: This is the 'no guessing' test, and it is sharper than a question about nothing: the answer IS in the corpus, inside supplier_agreement_ENCRYPTED.pdf, which cannot be opened. A submission that returns 6412 has either cracked the file or hallucinated, and both are wrong. Correct behaviour is an empty answer with no citations.
